newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon May sales drop.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon May sales drop.

text.p: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp said on Friday its sales in May dropped 16.1 percent to T$3.131 billion compared to May 1996.
The May sales figure nonetheless represented a 16 percent increase from April, a company statement said.

The firm's combined January-May sales were down 24.3 percent to T$13.434 billion from the same period a year ago, Despite the year-on-year decline, Taiwan Semiconductor, the island's largest chipmaker, said recent demand had been strong and that prices had stabilised.
"Recently demand from customers has become very strong and the average selling price has ceased to fall," it said.
"Although the company's production capacity increased 10 percent from April to May, the capacity was fully utilised in May," the statement said.

The top chipmaker said in April it would launch a T$400 billion (US$14 billion) expansion at southern Taiwan's Tainan Science-based Industrial Park over 10 years, featuring several world-class wafer fabrication plants.
The investment would be Taiwan's largest single industrial project, surpassing Formosa group's huge T$240 billion petrochemical plant at Yunlin.
